title: Butterfly Lighting
description: Butterfly lighting, also called Paramount lighting, places the key high and on the camera axis so a small butterfly-shaped shadow falls under the nose on the philtrum. Both cheeks stay open; both eyes take light.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: This is beauty lighting with a structure: cheekbones lift, the nose has a tidy shadow, and the face stays symmetrical for the lens. Classical glamour portraits used it because a star looking into camera still has modeling, not a flat flash.
It is the wrong tool for a liar in half-light, a bruised antihero, or anyone whose story is asymmetry. If you swing the key off axis, the butterfly becomes a loop.
If you raise it to the ceiling and kill the frontal component, you get top light sockets.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Center a large or medium source above the lens, aimed down at the face, high enough for the under-nose shadow but not so high the eye sockets collapse. A reflector under the chin is optional fill.
Hardness is usually soft to medium so skin wraps. Color is often tungsten or daylight beauty-neutral, not a green overhead.
Prompt: Key light high and centered on [Subject]'s face, a small shadow under the nose on the philtrum, both eyes open, glamour portrait.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for a glamour close-up, a singer facing camera, a studio beauty still. Do not use it on a crime profile that should be short-lit.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Loop lighting moves the key slightly off axis so the nose shadow slides toward the mouth corner. Rembrandt lighting is further off and higher, with a cheek triangle.
Glam is the broader beauty package (diffusion, catchlights) that often uses butterfly but does not have to. High-key lighting is frame contrast, not this nose-shadow pattern.
Top light is overhead enough to bury the eyes.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Classic Hollywood glamour, including Paramount-style portraits and films such as Gilda and Shanghai Express, parks the key high and frontal so the butterfly sits under the nose. The face stays a product the camera can sell.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is loop or top light. The tell is a nose shadow that leans to one side, or hollow eyes.
Fix it by centering the key and lowering it until sockets open and the butterfly sits on the philtrum.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is butterfly lighting in film?
A high, on-axis key that throws a small butterfly-shaped shadow under the nose. Both cheeks and both eyes stay lit. It is also called Paramount lighting.
Butterfly lighting vs loop lighting
Butterfly keeps the key centered; the nose shadow sits under the septum. Loop offsets the key so the shadow becomes a small loop toward the mouth, still not touching the cheek shadow.
When should I use butterfly lighting?
Use it for glamour and frontal beauty with a little structure. Skip it when the face should be secretive or half in shadow.
How do I prompt butterfly lighting for AI image or video?
Put the key high and centered. Ask for a small shadow under the nose on the philtrum, both eyes open, both cheeks lit.
